content.comment_body: Hello! Is there a way to manually set the network speed of [product_name] to 10 Mbit/s?
As far as I know, it is not possible to do this. Why do you need to change the network speed?

I am using a [product_name] CPU and six [product_name] modules connected via Ethernet switch using shielded FTP cables, all grounded at one point near the switch. The longest cable is 30 meters. Occasionally, the device farthest from the switch loses connection. The cables and connectors appear to be fine.

This might be due to differences in earth potential between devices. Did you connect the shield grounding to PE on your devices? If you did, try disconnecting it. Also, review your overall network grounding strategy. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion centers on network stability issues in a system containing multiple [product_name] modules. One user encounters intermittent connectivity loss on a device that's furthest from the switch and is considering adjusting Ethernet speed as a solution. The replies raise concerns about environmental grounding and clarify that manually changing network speed may not be supported by these devices.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is seeking an option to manually configure the Ethernet speed for [product_name] devices to potentially resolve network stability problems.
